title: Godot 4.6.2 headless can access-violate when project AppData paths are denied to process user on Windows
body:
### Summary

Godot 4.6.2 on Windows can crash with a native access violation when launched headless from a restricted/sandboxed Windows user where access to the normal Godot user-data/config paths is denied or restricted.

### Minimal Reproduction Observed

1. Run Godot from a restricted/sandboxed Windows user.
2. Launch:

```powershell
Godot_console.exe --headless --path <project> --quit
```

3. Observe an application error / access violation instead of a clean startup, clean shutdown, or readable permission error.

### Expected Behavior

Godot should either:

- start and quit successfully, or
- fail gracefully with a readable permission/configuration error.

### Actual Behavior

Godot exits via a native access violation dialog:

```text
The instruction at 0x00007FF659CA7CD4 referenced memory at 0x0000000000000058.
The memory could not be read.
```

### Environment

- Godot version: 4.6.2.stable.official.71f334935
- OS: Windows
- Launch mode: `Godot_console.exe --headless`
- Triggering condition observed: restricted/sandboxed Windows user context with denied/restricted access to normal Godot user-data/config locations.

### Additional Notes

Running the same `--headless --quit` command outside the restricted project/user context did not reproduce the crash. Running it inside the project from the restricted/sandboxed user context did reproduce the native access violation. The longer original report includes the environment comparison and logs that led us to suspect restricted user-data/config access as the trigger.
